1Password publishes the Events API as a downloadable OpenAPI 3.0.0 document (semver 1.4.1), linked from the Events API reference ("This API reference documents the latest version of the 1Password Events API specifications (1.4.1)"), which renders from it.

The 1Password Connect Server API likewise ships a downloadable OpenAPI document (3.0.2, version 1.8.1), linked from the Connect API reference as the specification file. The specs cover the Events and Connect surfaces; the Service Accounts/CLI/SDK surfaces are CLI/SDK-native without specs.

The Events API and Connect API references run the Mintlify interactive playground ("Try it" renders next to the endpoint, e.g. POST /api/v2/auditevents, with generated cURL samples). The CLI/SDK docs are prose and code only.

The Events API documents URL-path versioning with a continued-support commitment: "The Events API supports both V1 and V2 endpoints... V1 endpoints remain fully supported for existing integrations that don't require the additional MSP account and user type information", alongside a dedicated Events API changelog and a semver'd spec. This is an Events-API-specific policy; no account-wide or Connect-API deprecation policy page exists.

The implementation looks sound, and it's easy to use. Props to Agile Bits for making this feature a priority [Travel Mode].
I'm a very happy 1Password customer. Repeating my #1 feature request: logins keep breaking as websites evolve, change their forms, etc. Wish for an online catalog of login config/scripts.
Mandatory 'No Linux client' comment :| Does anyone have any insight if this is a pure business decision or there's something holding them back technically?
1Password fills iframes based on their domain rather than the parents... In my opinion this is the right security model.
Both the Fastmail and Privacy integrations have made 1Password a joy to use in the past few years. I've used premium BitWarden in the past, but the UX of 1Password is hard to beat.
My 1Password installation is grandfathered from a time when it was just a standalone app, without subscription. Will it just stop working one day to bully me into subscribing?
Use a tiny portion of that to continue support for local, non-cloud-based vault files please.
Except they have already started to diminish what used to make 1P great. We now get no native apps, no local vault storage, no upfront payments. The VC rot has already set in.
I've used 1password for years and so far haven't had any problem, all apps (desktop and mobile) work great, but I don't understand why they would need this kind of money.
It would be nice to say goodbye to Electron, though... (referring to 1Password's desktop app).
On 1Password Travel Mode: "The implementation looks sound, and it's easy to use. Props to Agile Bits for making this feature a priority."

"I'm a very happy 1Password customer." But their main problem is that saved logins keep breaking as websites change their forms. They want an online catalog of versioned login scripts with success-rate tracking.
Several users complained about the lack of a Linux client: "Mandatory 'No Linux client' comment" and "LINUX SUPPORT PLEASE. Seriously, please."
"Well darn, I guess I have to find a new password manager. 1Pass + Dropbox sync was so good." This was a reaction to 1Password 8 dropping local vaults.

1Password used to be a native Mac app and is now an Electron app. The commenter says they won't use it for that reason. They see subscription-only pricing plus non-native apps as signs of VC-driven decline.

Was unhappy with the move to subscription-only and tried Bitwarden. "After months of futzing around with it, I went back to 1password." Reasons: audit results, documented architecture and good Linux support. Sharing credentials with family is a big part of their use, and "1Password does a great job there."

Started with 1Password through a work account and added it for family. Says it has "definitely been an upgrade from LastPass in terms of usability and security (no random autofills into hidden forms, no breaches etc...)". Still sad to lose self-hosting as an option.

Very happy and fine paying the subscription; calls it the best password manager they've used. Says it makes sharing with their wife seamless. Doesn't mind Electron since they mostly use the browser extension. Also likes the CLI tool for accessing passwords.

Standalone user for about a decade who finds the change "incredibly disappointing". Doesn't mind a subscription fee. But: "either they give us a self-hosted option or I'm done with 1password. Keeping my passwords in someone else's cloud is a red line for me."

Happy user for over a decade who switched to the subscription happily. Uses it on many devices, so buying standalone licenses for each "cost more than the sub does." Not bothered by Electron since 99% of use is via mobile or the browser plugin.
Says the Fastmail masked-email and Privacy virtual-card integrations "have made 1Password a joy to use". Has used premium Bitwarden before, "but the UX of 1Password is hard to beat."

Still recommends 1Password over Bitwarden to non-tech people: "their whole UX journey is so well crafted that even my parents can understand it on their own." Pays for Bitwarden but finds its UI clunky.

Loves it for business and personal use; finds shared family vaults important for emergencies. Complaints: it's expensive and has no easy way to share a URL with a client. The "new" button is barely visible. Two-factor setup was buggy, and there have been no major functional updates in about 2 years. "But it's the best for now."

12-year user whose mother has used 1Password for 9 years and uses its QR-code 2FA capture. The classic browser extension was hard to find when reinstalling. Customer support's response was to upgrade to a paid account and store passwords on a server. Wants the native Mac app and Dropbox-based licenses to stay.
"The horrible Linux support they had was the reason I left 1Password." Says the Linux preview might bring them back.
"1Password has probably been the single biggest productivity increase tool I've ever purchased. Worth every cent."

Moved from paid 1Password to Bitwarden over the lack of Linux support. Couldn't export passwords on Linux because only the desktop apps support export, and it wouldn't run under Wine. Had to install a Windows VM just to do the export.
Uses 1Password professionally with company-wide shared vaults by department and security level. Also uses it at home to share credentials with their wife. "Absolutely love it."
Uses 1Password at work and Bitwarden personally. Finds 1Password "awkward and often counterintuitive" compared with Bitwarden.

Says 1Password's UI hasn't been matched yet, which matters for getting less technical people to use it. Regrets the push away from local control toward subscriptions. Wants hardware-token unlock in the local apps.
